program_meta.advisor_model: TUM (and Germany generally) is CHAIR-BASED ('Lehrstuhl' system), fundamentally different from the US department/rotation model. Each full professor ('Lehrstuhlinhaber') heads their OWN independent chair with its own budget, PhD/postdoc/HiWi (student-assistant) positions, and hiring authority - there is no central CS department that assigns advisors. A doctoral position at TUM is NOT a program admission with coursework; it is almost always a PAID EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT (Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter, usually TV-L E13, 50-100%) or a scholarship, offered by a specific chair when that chair has funding and an open slot - functionally like being hired for a research-assistant job, not 'admitted to a PhD program'. Consequently: (1) there is no unified TUM PhD application portal comparable to US CS PhD apps; (2) prospective doctoral students must find an individual professor with an open, funded position (via the chair's own website 'join us' / 'open positions' page, via a TUM Graduate School listing, or via direct email) and be hired into that specific chair; (3) enrollment in the TUM Doctoral Studies framework (via TUM Graduate School) happens AFTER a chair has agreed to supervise, not before. For a Master's student hoping to reach a specific chair for a thesis: master's thesis supervision is arranged individually with a chair, typically by taking that chair's courses/seminars first, doing a 'Guided Research' module or an Interdisciplinary Project with them, or directly emailing the professor/a senior PhD student in the group to ask about thesis or HiWi (studentische Hilfskraft, part-time paid research-assistant) capacity - there is no formal centralized matching process. The MSc Informatics program page explicitly lists a 'Guided Research' module with its own dedicated contact address (gr-in.asa@xcit.tum.de), which is the closest thing to an official channel for connecting a master's student to a specific chair.
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, structurally built into the degree via two mechanisms named on the program page: (1) 'Guided Research' - a formal module for students to do supervised research with a chair during the Master's, with its own coordination email; (2) 'Interdisciplinary Project in an Application Subject' - a project module. The Master's thesis ('Final Thesis') itself is also done within a specific chair. Program coordinator for academic questions: Dr. Wolfgang Woerndl (woerndl@in.tum.de). Getting INTO a specific chair for these is informal/direct-contact based, per advisor_model above - there is no guarantee of placement with any named professor.
program_meta.notes: STRUCTURE CORRECTION vs the user's brief: 'MSc Informatics (Machine Learning & Data Engineering track)' is not a formally named track on TUM's own program page - Informatics MSc offers flexible specialization across 'at least one of eight computer science specializations' (exact list of the 8 was not enumerated in the fetched page) rather than a fixed named ML/Data-Engineering track; ML-flavored specialization is achieved via elective module choice. TUM ALSO separately offers a distinctly-named 'Master Data Engineering and Analytics' program (own page: https://www.cit.tum.de/en/cit/studies/degree-programs/master-data-engineering-and-analytics/, NOT independently fetched this pass) which is the closer literal match to 'MSc Data Engineering and Analytics' named in the user's target - these are TWO DIFFERENT DEGREES with likely different admission pages/deadlines; decide which one to apply to and verify its own page separately.
